method.method_draft: First describe the circuit in the image: the right half is the control ladder of an automatic forward/reverse circuit, with numbered terminals, SB1 in the start/control branch, SQ1 contacts in the position-switch branch, and KM1/KM2 coils at the lower part. From the text, set the operation sequence: meter across 0 and 1, keep SB1 pressed, then operate SQ1 and release it back. Trace the completed branch with SB1 pressed: the meter sees a completed contactor-coil circuit, so the reading corresponds to the contactor circuit resistance. When SQ1 is toggled, its contact state momentarily changes the completed branch and interrupts/adds resistance in that path, so the displayed resistance briefly rises. When SQ1 returns to its original position, the original coil path is restored, so the reading returns to the contactor circuit resistance.

method.method_draft: Model the control ladder as contact logic. Treat SB1 pressed as a closed start contact. Treat the original SQ1 position as one Boolean state and the manually toggled SQ1 position as the opposite state for its linked contacts. For each state, reduce the circuit between terminals 0 and 1 to an equivalent resistance: with SB1 held and SQ1 in the original state, one contactor branch is enabled, so the equivalent is the contactor circuit resistance. During the manual SQ1 change, the enable condition for the original branch is briefly disrupted, so the equivalent resistance increases. After SQ1 is returned, the original Boolean state and the original contactor branch are restored, so the meter reading goes back to the contactor circuit resistance.
